text:
Alex Kim: Heads up — found wrapped KMS ciphertext blobs in a partner S3 backup that look like staging DB creds. Not plaintext, but partner had decrypt calls. Object: s3://partner-backups/2026-03-22/db-backup.enc. Affected: staging only (so far).
Maria Chen: Can you paste the object key + a snippet of metadata so we can confirm KMS key id and principal? Also tag partner contact.
Alex Kim: Metadata excerpt: key: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/staging/cryptoKeys/staging-db-wrap-1, wrapped_by: partner-app-v1, x-amz-meta-author=backup-agent. I pulled headers and attached manifest to ticket.
Jenna Patel: If partner had unwrapping access, treat as potential compromise. Start credential rotation for any services using that DB user. Plan to rewrap all ciphertext to our new key and revoke partner grants.
Sam Ortiz: Agreed. High-level steps: 1) isolate S3 prefix (block presigned URLs / bucket policy), 2) snapshot list of objects, 3) provision new KMS key, 4) rewrap ciphertext to new key, 5) rotate DB passwords and update Secret Manager. Who can run rewrap? I can take the object snapshot and do the canary.
Alex Kim: I started a manifest export: gs://redwood-eng-incident/1795012345-manifest.json. Audit logs show partner service account used Decrypt on that key at 2026-03-22T04:12Z.
secbot: Audit alert: KMS key grant 'partner-sa@partner.iam' used for Decrypt on key 'staging-db-wrap-1'. See /incidents/1795012345 for details.
Maria Chen: Revoke the grant ASAP and rekey. Security runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-wrap-exposure (read-only). Suggest a canary rotation for one microservice before wide rollout.
Jenna Patel: I'll open an RBAC PR to remove the partner binding from the staging key ring + add a deny rule where supported. We'll need emergency approval.
Sam Ortiz: Commands I'll run from a secure ephemeral host (pseudo): ```bash
# list objects
aws s3 ls s3://partner-backups/2026-03-22/ --recursive > /tmp/manifest
# copy objects to sealed host
aws s3 cp s3://partner-backups/2026-03-22/ /tmp/backups --recursive
# create new key (example)
gcloud kms keys create staging-db-wrap-2 --location global --keyring staging --purpose=encryption
# rewrap loop (pseudo, do not leave plaintext on disk)
for f in /tmp/backups/*.enc; do
  gcloud kms decrypt --location global --keyring staging --key staging-db-wrap-1 --ciphertext-file=$f --plaintext-file=$f.dec
  gcloud kms encrypt --location global --keyring staging --key staging-db-wrap-2 --plaintext-file=$f.dec --ciphertext-file=$f.rewrapped
done
```
Alex Kim: Important: DO NOT decrypt to persistent disk in production. Use an ephemeral sealed host or memory pipes and wipe any plaintext immediately. Ensure new key is HSM-backed and has strict IAM.
Maria Chen: I'll coordinate with Product for deploy windows. Sam, estimate timeline for a full sweep vs a canary?
Sam Ortiz: Estimate: manifest + snapshot 30m, canary rewrap 45m, full rewrap for ~20GB ~3-4h depending on IO, credential rotations + deploys ~1-2h. Target mitigation window < 8h.
Jenna Patel: I'll queue the RBAC PR and request emergency approval from security lead; adding remediation steps to the runbook.
Drew Lawson: Drew Lawson (oncall): ACK. Approve immediate revoke of partner grant and canary rotation. Keep me updated. Create incident ticket and post to #incidents once grants are revoked.
Alex Kim: Already created INCIDENT-1795012345 and notified partner. Current status: manifest exported, partner notified, waiting for RBAC revoke approval.
secbot: Deploy-bot: rotation job queued in infra-jobs (job-87123).
Sam Ortiz: Starting canary rewrap now on ephemeral host. Hitting KMS rate limit, throttling parallelism to 10. Will post success snippet when complete.
Alex Kim: Also run an audit query for other uses by partner SA: `gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt" AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail:partner-sa@partner.com' --project=redwood-infra`
Maria Chen: Checklist for closure: revoke grant, perform rewrap, rotate credentials, update Secret Manager with new ciphertexts, run integration tests, hold old key for 24h observation, then schedule key destroy after postmortem. Add vendor SLA review.
Drew Lawson: Good plan. After containment we'll run a short postmortem and vendor security review. Thanks team — keep updates in INCIDENT-1795012345 and #incidents.
